A.explanation: Divides $1.7$ by $53$ instead of $0.53$, which treats $53\%$ as $53$ and gives an output far too small.

B.explanation: Multiplies input $1.7\text{ kW}$ by $0.53$, giving about $0.90\text{ kW}$ of useful power.

C.explanation: Divides $1.7\text{ kW}$ by $0.53$, which gives power output larger than power input and is impossible for efficiency below $100\%$.

D.explanation: Multiplies $1.7$ by $53$ without converting $53\%$ to $0.53$, giving $90\text{ kW}$ with wrong magnitude.

hints: Notice the motor takes in $1.7\text{ kW}$ and only $53\%$ of that becomes useful output power.
Recall efficiency for power is $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful output power} / \text{input power}$.
Convert $53\%$ to $0.53$ then multiply by $1.7\text{ kW}$ to find the useful part, which must be less than $1.7\text{ kW}$.
walkthrough: Identify the input power $P_{in} = 1.7\text{ kW}$ and the efficiency $53\% = 0.53$.
State the rule for efficiency using power: $\text{efficiency} = P_{useful} / P_{in}$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $0.53 \times 1.7 = 0.901$, so $P_{useful} \approx 0.90\text{ kW}$, which is less than the input as expected. This is option B.
